chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him, who said:
If the mother of the child (umm al-walad) kills her master by mistake, she is freed and there is no blood money (diyah) upon her.
And Wahb ibn Wahb narrated from Ja'far, from his father, that he used to say:
If the umm al-walad kills her master by mistake, she is freed and there is no penalty upon her; and if she kills him intentionally, she is executed for it.
As for what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Abu Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ja'far, from his father, who said:
If the umm al-walad kills her master by mistake, she pays the value (of her freedom) from herself; this does not contradict the first two narrations.

Because the meaning in the first two narrations is that we interpret them as applying when her child is still alive; for if her master dies, she is freed from her child's share. The other narration is interpreted as applying to one who has no child; she is freed from his share, so the heirs should pay her off if they wish, and if they wish to sell her, they have that right.

key_terms.أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ: Female slave who bears her master's child
key_terms.سَعَايَةٌ: Payment of value/price (specifically for freeing a slave)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an umm al-walad who kills her master by mistake or intentionally?
ai.summary: This passage from *Al-Istibsar* highlights the Shia scholarly method of *jam'* (reconciliation) to resolve apparent contradictions between narrations regarding the *umm al-walad*. It distinguishes between accidental and intentional homicide, noting that while accidental killing typically results in freedom without execution, the heirs retain the option to pay her value or sell her, particularly depending on whether her child survives to inherit. This legal nuance underscores the interplay between manumission rights and inheritance laws in classical Shia jurisprudence.
